6114.t: From συγγιγνώσκω (sŭngĭgnṓskō, “to agree with; to acknowledge; to excuse; to pardon”) + -μη (-mē); by surface analysis, συν- (sŭn-) + γνώμη (gnṓmē).

6131.t: From σύμφωνος (sŭ́mphōnos, “agreeing in sound, harmonious”) + -ία (-ĭ́ā) and συν- (sŭn-, “with, together”) + -φωνία (-phōníā, “sound”).

6197.t: Neuter accusative plural of ταχύς (tăkhŭ́s, “quick”) used as adverb.

6158.t: The formation is similar to δάκτυλος (dáktulos) and κόνδυλος (kóndulos), probably first from a noun *σφόνδος (*sphóndos).

6199.t: From Proto-Indo-European *térmn̥, the same source of Latin terminus (“boundary, limit, end”).

6195.t: From Proto-Hellenic *tūrós (whence also Mycenaean Greek 𐀶𐀫 (tu-ro /⁠tūrós⁠/)), probably from Proto-Indo-European *tuh₂-ró-s, from *tewh₂- (“to swell”).

6168.t: From συντάσσω (suntássō, “to put together”) + -μα (-ma) and συν- (sun-) + τάγμα (tágma, “command, order”)

6136.t: From the aorist stem of συντρέχω (suntrékhō) + -η (-ē, verbal noun suffix).

6149.t: From συναλλάσσω (sŭnăllắssō, “to have dealings with another”) + -μα (-ma). By surface analysis, συν- (sun-, “syn-, with”) + ἄλλαγμα (állagma, “something taken in exchange”).

6174.t: From τεῖχος (teîkhos, “wall, fortification”) + -ίζω (-ĭ́zō, suffix used to form verbs from nouns, adjectives and other verbs).

6189.t: From τροπαῖος (tropaîos, “of defeat”), from τροπή (tropḗ, “rout, turning of an enemy”).

6196.t: From Proto-Hellenic *tótsos, earlier *tótyos, from Proto-Indo-European *tóti, adverb from *só. Cognate with Sanskrit तति (táti), Latin tot.

6120.t: From σῦκον (sûkon, “fig”) + φαίνω (phaínō, “show”) + -της (-tēs, masculine agent-noun suffix).

6182.t: From τοῖος (toîos, “such”) + -δε (-de, deictic suffix). Compare ὅδε (hóde, “this here”).

6121.t: Verbal noun from συλλογίζομαι (sullogízomai, “to compute, infer”) + -μός (-mós).

6157.t: Unknown. Has been linked to Sanskrit स्फ्य (sphyá, “oar; spar”) and Proto-Germanic *spēnuz (“chip; shaving”), but this is phonologically impossible due to the aspirated labial /pʰ/ in Greek.

6111.t: Late Hellenistic Koine back-formation from ἕστηκα (héstēkă, “I have stood”), perfect of ἵστημι (hĭ́stēmĭ).

6106.t: Maybe from Proto-Indo-European *strebʰ- (“to twist”), which στρέφω (stréphō, “to twist”) is also often derived from.

6110.t: From στυγέω (stugéō) + -νός (-nós), of uncertain origin, possibly from Proto-Indo-European *(s)tewg- (“to hit, push”) (compare Sanskrit तुज् (tuj, “to push, drive”)).

6156.t: Conventionally connected with Proto-Indo-European *sperH-, although Pre-Greek, according to Beekes.

6169.t: Possibly from Proto-Indo-European *ten- (“to stretch”); related to τείνω (teínō, “to stretch”). Cognate with Serbo-Croatian тѐтива, Slovene tetiva (< Proto-Slavic *tętiva), Polish ścięgno.

6175.t: From Proto-Indo-European *telh₂- (“to bear”) + -μων (-mōn), as its original meaning was "bearer".

6100.t: From στείβω (steíbō, “to tread, stamp”) + -η (-ē). The "cushion" and "padding" senses are from the custom of filling pillows and mattresses using shrub leaves.

6124.t: Etymology tree Ancient Greek συν- (sŭn-) Ancient Greek πάσχω (páskhō)der.

6108.t: From Proto-Hellenic *stugéō, from Proto-Indo-European *stug-éyeti, from *(s)tewg- (“to push, hit”).

6190.t: Enlargement of τρύω (trúō), in the same manner as terms such as σμήχω (smḗkhō).
